correctness.rationale: The real skew matrix J=M/a squares to −I and has conjugate complex eigenspaces, so the Euclidean product-norm computation splits into identical-norm B and conjugate B blocks. The real induced norm equals the complexified norm: writing a complex input as x+iy splits both squared norms into sums of real squared norms. Direct subtraction of λ=(1−i)/2 from B gives a nonzero rank-one N with N²=0, trace zero and Frobenius square 1. Thus B^k=λ^k(I+kN/λ), and the latter parenthesized matrix has determinant 1 and squared Frobenius norm 2+2k². Solving the quadratic for its squared singular values gives 1+k²+k√(k²+2), proving the exact power norm and the asymptotic coefficient 2. The finite candidates 0,1,2 are smaller than k=3; in particular 99>96 verifies the k=3 versus k=2 radical comparison. For k≥4 the monotone upper bound 2^(−k)(2k²+2) starts at 34/16, below the k=3 value. On a synchronized modal vector (w,w), the two components of N(w,w) are (λw, conjugate(λ)w); dividing by λ gives the stated primal and auxiliary powers, and the consecutive primal squared-gain ratio drops below 1 exactly when k≥2. The weak 3/4 bound from the DGDA reference is compatible. The sharper general inequality printed in the same reference, at its repeated-root endpoint, is not compatible; the frozen statement carefully refers to the weaker bound only.
residual_risks: The uploaded script was inspected, not executed. Its frozen 209-check output is not an all-dimension or all-horizon certificate. The analytical modal reduction and tail bound establish those quantifiers.
